claims.text: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 exhibits a ductile-brittle-ductile transition when aged between 550 and 750°C, with a brittle state near 600°C and recovered ductility near 750°C.
The transition is driven by coupled evolution of L12 ordered domains and jagged B2/FCC interfaces.
Aging near 600°C produces excessive Ni3Al-like chemical ordering in the FCC matrix.
The ordering near 600°C raises the antiphase-boundary energy above 100 mJ/m².
The ordering near 600°C reduces the stacking-fault energy.
High APBE and low SFE restrict dislocation cross-slip and promote planar slip.
Planar slip creates stress concentrations at jagged phase-boundary serrations, initiating brittle cracks.
At approximately 750°C, reduced chemical order lowers APBE and restores dislocation cross-slip and plasticity.
Aging near 750°C forms ductile transition zones along phase boundaries.
The as-cast alloy has a nanolamellar FCC/B2 microstructure.
The FCC constituent of the as-cast material is L12 ordered.
The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy is ductile.
The relevant B2/FCC phase boundaries are jagged and have high interfacial energy.
The brittle window near 600°C is flanked by ductile states below 550°C and above 750°C.
The as-cast FCC matrix is chemically random.
The as-cast B2/FCC interfaces are smooth.
The critical brittle-transition boundary occurs when the Ni3Al-like L12 order parameter exceeds approximately 0.8, corresponding to APBE above 100 mJ/m².
The critical order parameter and APBE threshold vary with local composition and aging time.
Magnetic effects omitted by non-spin-polarized EAM potentials may influence the relevant energy barriers.
Relative to the 750°C sample, the 600°C sample should exhibit higher APBE, more jagged phase boundaries, higher local hardness, and reduced nanoindentation pile-up.

contradictions.description: The initial-state field describes the as-cast FCC constituent as L12 ordered, whereas the baseline describes the same as-cast FCC matrix as chemically random.
